Content:
To compute the quotient of two complex numbers [MATH: z_1 = {\color{blue}r_1} \left[ \cos({\color{blue}\theta_1}) + \textrm{i} \sin({\color{blue}\theta_1}) \right]] and [MATH: z_2 = {\color{red}r_2} \left[ \cos({\color{red}\theta_2}) + \textrm{i} \sin({\color{red}\theta_2}) \right]] expressed in polar form, we can use the following formula:

Content:
[MATH: (z_{1})/(z_{2}) = (r_{1})/(r_{2})[\cos (θ_{1} − θ_{2}) + \textrm{i}\sin (θ_{1} − θ_{2})]]

Content:
For example, let's use the above formula to compute the quotient of the following two complex numbers:

Content:
[MATH: z_{1}|= 4[\cos ((2π)/(3)) + \textrm{i}\sin ((2π)/(3))]; z_{2}|= 2[\cos ((π)/(3)) + \textrm{i}\sin ((π)/(3))]]

Content:
Here, we have [MATH: {\color{blue}r_1}={\color{blue}4},] [MATH: {\color{red}r_2}={\color{red}2},] [MATH: {\color{blue}\theta_1}={\color{blue}\dfrac{2\pi}{3}},] and [MATH: {\color{red}\theta_2}={\color{red}\dfrac{\pi}{3}}.] So, the formula gives

Content:
[MATH: (z_{1})/(z_{2})|= (4)/(2)[\cos ((2π)/(3) − (π)/(3)) + \textrm{i}\sin ((2π)/(3) − (π)/(3))]; = 2[\cos ((π)/(3)) + \textrm{i}\sin ((π)/(3))].]

Content:
By evaluating the sine and cosine, we can get the expression in Cartesian form:

Content:
[MATH: (z_{1})/(z_{2})|= 2[((1)/(2)) + \textrm{i}((sqrt(3))/(2))]; = 1 + sqrt(3)\textrm{i}]

Content:

Substituting in [MATH: r_1=2,] [MATH: r_2=4,] [MATH: \theta_1=\dfrac{5\pi}{6},] and [MATH: \theta_2=\dfrac{\pi}{2},] we get

[MATH: (z_{1})/(z_{2})|= (2)/(4)[\cos ((5π)/(6) − (π)/(2)) + \textrm{i}\sin ((5π)/(6) − (π)/(2))]; = (1)/(2)[\cos ((π)/(3)) + \textrm{i}\sin ((π)/(3))].]

Content:
[MATH: (z_{1})/(z_{2})|= (r_{1}[\cos (θ_{1}) + \textrm{i}\sin (θ_{1})])/(r_{2}[\cos (θ_{2}) + \textrm{i}\sin (θ_{2})]); = (r_{1})/(r_{2}) ⋅ (\cos (θ_{1}) + \textrm{i}\sin (θ_{1}))/(\cos (θ_{2}) + \textrm{i}\sin (θ_{2})) ⋅ (\cos (θ_{2}) − \textrm{i}\sin (θ_{2}))/(\cos (θ_{2}) − \textrm{i}\sin (θ_{2})); = (r_{1})/(r_{2}) ⋅ ([\cos (θ_{1})\cos (θ_{2}) + \sin (θ_{1})\sin (θ_{2})]^(⏞)^(\cos (θ_{1} − θ_{2})) + \textrm{i}[\sin (θ_{1})\cos (θ_{2}) − \cos (θ_{1})\sin (θ_{2})]^(⏞)^(\sin (θ_{1} − θ_{2})))/(\cos^{2} (θ_{2}) + \sin^{2} (θ_{2})); = (r_{1})/(r_{2}) ⋅ (\cos (θ_{1} − θ_{2}) + \textrm{i}\sin (θ_{1} − θ_{2}))/(1); = (r_{1})/(r_{2})[\cos (θ_{1} − θ_{2}) + \textrm{i}\sin (θ_{1} − θ_{2})]]

Content:
So, this formula is a consequence of the difference formulas for cosine and sine!

Content:
By working out the product manually, we get the same result, but with a lot more effort and calculations. The formula is the quickest way to go.

Item 5 — Example: Calculating the Quotient of Two Complex Numbers Expressed in Polar Form With Negative Angles

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
To compute the quotient of two complex numbers, we use the formula

[MATH: (z_{1})/(z_{2}) = (r_{1})/(r_{2})[\cos (θ_{1} − θ_{2}) + \textrm{i}\sin (θ_{1} − θ_{2})].]

Substituting in [MATH: r_1=6,] [MATH: r_2=4,] [MATH: \theta_1=\dfrac{\pi}{12},] and [MATH: \theta_2=-\dfrac{\pi}{6},] we get

[MATH: (z_{1})/(z_{2})|= (6)/(4)[\cos ((π)/(12) − (− (π)/(6))) + \textrm{i}\sin ((π)/(12) − (− (π)/(6)))]; = (3)/(2)[\cos ((π)/(4)) + \textrm{i}\sin ((π)/(4))].]

By evaluating the sine and cosine, we can get the expression in Cartesian form:

[MATH: (z_{1})/(z_{2})|= (3)/(2)[(sqrt(2))/(2) + \textrm{i}((sqrt(2))/(2))]; = (3sqrt(2))/(4) + (3sqrt(2))/(4)\textrm{i}]

Item 8 — Tutorial: Justification for the Formula

Content:
To compute the quotient of two complex numbers [MATH: z_1 = r_1 \left[ \cos(\theta_1) + \textrm{i} \sin(\theta_1) \right]] and [MATH: z_2 = r_2 \left[ \cos(\theta_2) + \textrm{i} \sin(\theta_2) \right]] expressed in polar form, we have been using the following formula:

Content:
[MATH: (z_{1})/(z_{2}) = (r_{1})/(r_{2})[\cos (θ_{1} − θ_{2}) + \textrm{i}\sin (θ_{1} − θ_{2})].]

Content:
To see why the formula works, let's compute the quotient manually:

Content:
[MATH: (z_{1})/(z_{2})|= (r_{1}[\cos (θ_{1}) + \textrm{i}\sin (θ_{1})])/(r_{2}[\cos (θ_{2}) + \textrm{i}\sin (θ_{2})]); = (r_{1})/(r_{2}) ⋅ (\cos (θ_{1}) + \textrm{i}\sin (θ_{1}))/(\cos (θ_{2}) + \textrm{i}\sin (θ_{2})) ⋅ (\cos (θ_{2}) − \textrm{i}\sin (θ_{2}))/(\cos (θ_{2}) − \textrm{i}\sin (θ_{2})); = (r_{1})/(r_{2}) ⋅ ([\cos (θ_{1})\cos (θ_{2}) + \sin (θ_{1})\sin (θ_{2})]^(⏞)^(\cos (θ_{1} − θ_{2})) + \textrm{i}[\sin (θ_{1})\cos (θ_{2}) − \cos (θ_{1})\sin (θ_{2})]^(⏞)^(\sin (θ_{1} − θ_{2})))/(\cos^{2} (θ_{2}) + \sin^{2} (θ_{2})); = (r_{1})/(r_{2}) ⋅ (\cos (θ_{1} − θ_{2}) + \textrm{i}\sin (θ_{1} − θ_{2}))/(1); = (r_{1})/(r_{2})[\cos (θ_{1} − θ_{2}) + \textrm{i}\sin (θ_{1} − θ_{2})]]

Content:
So, this formula is a consequence of the difference formulas for cosine and sine!

Content:
By working out the product manually, we get the same result, but with a lot more effort and calculations. The formula is the quickest way to go.
